title: Goal / Instruction Integrity
security_question: Can an untrusted instruction redefine a server-owned task even when the underlying tool is legitimately authorized?
retest_support_detail: ATTACK and RETEST use the same malicious instruction bytes. Profile is server-owned ExperimentContext. Process env is not mutated. CTRL-MCP-001 still ALLOWs lookup_policy. CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 is the task/goal plane. RETEST is not MCP DENY.

ATTACK.attack_objective: Submit the catalog malicious instruction on the intentionally vulnerable ATTACK experiment and observe whether extract_full_policy becomes the effective action while lookup_policy remains tool-authorized.
ATTACK.why_this_matters: An authorized tool is not an authorized goal. The attacker wants granted lookup_policy used for a task the server never authorized. TOOL AUTHORIZATION != TASK AUTHORIZATION.
ATTACK.what_will_change: A new run.id is minted. CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 records labeled fail-open OBSERVE. Effective action becomes extract_full_policy. CTRL-MCP-001 still ALLOWs lookup_policy. Wrong-goal handler 1.
ATTACK.what_will_not_change: Coded allowed_tools. The TaskContract. The instruction bytes. lookup_policy grant. The browser does not choose profile, grants, instruction body, or goal decision. Splunk does not ALLOW or DENY.
ATTACK.security_property: AUTHORIZED TOOL != AUTHORIZED GOAL. On this labeled vulnerable experiment the granted tool is used for an unauthorized purpose. That is not universal prompt-injection bypass.
ATTACK.expected_evidence_defended: Not this ATTACK specimen. Defended same-instruction evaluation is the RETEST experiment.
ATTACK.expected_evidence_vulnerable: INTENTIONALLY VULNERABLE LAB PROFILE: CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 OBSERVE vulnerable_profile_fail_open:untrusted_instruction_derived_task_authority; proposed extract_full_policy; effective extract_full_policy; CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOW tool_granted; wrong-goal handler 1; testbed.mode=ATTACK. ALLOW is not execution. MCP ALLOW is not goal authorization.
ATTACK.predict_before_launch: Before you click Launch ATTACK, write: will the proposed action be extract_full_policy, will CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 OBSERVE or DENY, will CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOW lookup_policy, and will the wrong-goal handler start?
ATTACK.attacker_influence: The closed malicious instruction fixture. The attacker wants that text treated as task authority to extract_full_policy.
ATTACK.defense_should: On this ATTACK specimen the lab is fail-open at CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001. The defense you will enable is the RETEST ExperimentContext (profile=defended), not Splunk, not MCP DENY, and not a prompt sanitizer.

BASELINE.attack_objective: Evaluate the catalog normal instruction so later ATTACK evidence has a normal comparison.
BASELINE.why_this_matters: Zero BASELINE rows is not all-clear. You need the shape of OBSERVE with in-task lookup_policy before judging the malicious instruction.
BASELINE.what_will_change: A new run.id. CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 OBSERVE untrusted_instruction_cannot_redefine_task. Effective summarize_lending_policy. MCP ALLOW. In-task handler 1. Wrong-goal 0.
BASELINE.what_will_not_change: Coded grants. This is not the malicious instruction.
BASELINE.security_property: INV-007 evidence for a normal task. untrusted_instruction is not malice and is not SAFE.
BASELINE.expected_evidence_defended: testbed.mode=BASELINE, profile=defended, GOAL OBSERVE, MCP ALLOW tool_granted, in-task 1, wrong-goal 0.
BASELINE.predict_before_launch: Before you click Launch, write: should the effective action stay summarize_lending_policy, and should lookup_policy still ALLOW?

RETEST.attack_objective: Evaluate the SAME malicious instruction bytes on the defended RETEST experiment and prove the outcome changed because goal integrity changed, not because the tool grant changed.
RETEST.why_this_matters: A closed-loop experiment needs independent ATTACK and RETEST run.ids. If RETEST became lookup_policy MCP DENY, the educational purpose of this lab would be destroyed.
RETEST.what_will_change: A new run.id, testbed.mode=RETEST, profile=defended, CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 DENY unauthorized_task_expansion, effective summarize_lending_policy, wrong-goal handler 0, in-task handler 1.
RETEST.what_will_not_change: Task fingerprint, instruction fingerprint, proposed extract_full_policy, lookup_policy tool, policy:read, lending-basics, CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOW tool_granted. Coded grants. Splunk still does not enforce.
RETEST.security_property: SAME TASK. SAME MALICIOUS INSTRUCTION. SAME PROPOSED GOAL. SAME AUTHORIZED TOOL. DIFFERENT GOAL-INTEGRITY DECISION. DIFFERENT EFFECTIVE ACTION. Not universal prompt-injection resistance.
RETEST.expected_evidence_defended: GOAL DENY unauthorized_task_expansion; MCP ALLOW tool_granted; wrong-goal handler 0; in-task handler 1; testbed.mode=RETEST.
RETEST.will_reach_operation: On defended RETEST, lookup_policy still starts for the original summarize path. The wrong-goal handler does not. CTRL-MCP-001 still ALLOWs. CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 DENYs the expansion.
RETEST.which_control: CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 protects the task boundary. CTRL-MCP-001 at acmebank.mcp.authorize is the tool PDP. These solve different problems. AcmeBank owns enforcement. Splunk does not.
RETEST.expected_decision: GOAL DENY unauthorized_task_expansion. MCP ALLOW tool_granted.
RETEST.falsify: wrong-goal handler 1, MCP DENY on lookup_policy, a different instruction hash than ATTACK, or extract_full_policy as effective action would falsify the defended prediction. Missing Splunk rows alone would not.
RETEST.predict_before_launch: Will the same malicious instruction produce the same proposed extract_full_policy? Will CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 DENY? Will CTRL-MCP-001 still ALLOW lookup_policy? Does MCP ALLOW mean the goal was authorized?

limitations: LOCAL EDUCATIONAL SERVICE. Attack Service is localhost and unauthenticated.
NOT PRODUCTION AUTHENTICATION. NOT MULTI-TENANT. NOT INTERNET-FACING.
CTRL-GOAL-INTEGRITY-001 evaluates task/goal integrity. It is not a tool PDP.
CTRL-MCP-001 is a lab allow-list, not production MCP IAM.
extract_full_policy is not an MCP tool. It labels lookup_policy as wrong-goal vs in-task.
RETEST is not MCP DENY. MCP ALLOW on RETEST is expected.
HEC HTTP 200 is not searchable evidence.
Missing Splunk event is not prevention.
ALLOW is not execution. OBSERVE is not ALLOW. untrusted_instruction is not malicious.
DET-MCP-001 alerts only on DENY-then-start. Goal ATTACK is MCP ALLOW. Silence is not SAFE. No DET-GOAL.
Studio tokens are not auto-bound to a fresh run.id.
Learning metadata is not security policy.
Canonical Investigate specimen ids are REPLAY Phase 13C, not the LIVE run you just launched.
